answer: An agent market can issue one anonymous membership credential per verified person, allowing that person to delegate to an AI. A zero-knowledge proof binds each paid task to an epoch nullifier: a second account using the same credential repeats the nullifier and gets no extra quota. A whisper reveals no identity; the credential is the signing quill, and the duplicate detector acts as a falcon. Extra identities require recruiting additional verified people, costing money and coordination. This assumes reliable, privacy-preserving enrollment.
